A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison after matching the CrossAgent-to-CrossHA rename and relocated case studies.

before.justification: v1 reports original Minecraft evaluations, training ablations, ID/OOD comparisons, and agent rollouts in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original evaluations and ablations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–4, with case-study results moved to Appendix E.

M1.justification: CrossAgent is renamed CrossHA, but the mixed-space SFT, STRL, self-training initialization, and MTRL procedures remain unchanged. The rewards, objectives, and action-selection mechanism are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Minecraft/OpenHA coverage: 30 RL training tasks and over 800 evaluation tasks spanning mining, combat, and crafting. The training-data sources and three case-study tasks are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 and the ablation plots is unchanged. OpenHA and Game-TARS receive expanded descriptions in v2, but both already appear in v1's Table 1.

E3.justification: The reported model configuration, training budgets, 200-step ablation cold start, ID/OOD evaluation, and FT/ASR metrics remain unchanged. Omitted descriptions of ablation controls do not establish changed experimental procedures.

E4.justification: The mixed-action-space and STRL ablations, ID/OOD analysis, and three behavioral case studies are retained. Moving Section 4.5 to Appendix E adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same standard-deviation reporting, and the action-density case studies still aggregate 20 episodes. No new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 are numerically unchanged, including overall ASR of 54.6% and overall OOD success of 49.1% for the proposed model. Training curves, action-density plots, and qualitative rollout findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The composite-action-space formulation, reward definitions, objectives in Equations 1–6, and GRPO formulations in Appendix C remain unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and shortened conclusion retain the same central contributions: learned action-space switching, the staged GRPO pipeline, and claimed performance, efficiency, and generalization benefits on Minecraft.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 removes the specific interpretation that STRL prevents policy collapse into suboptimal modes, retaining the narrower conclusion that it improves generalization. The conclusion also compresses the computational-cost and robotics-transfer discussion, omitting specific offline-RL suggestions.

D1.justification: v2 omits Section 4.3's explicit statements that cold-start samples were not repeated and that the STRL ablation received identical MTRL training. Hardware, software, Table 4 hyperparameters, and code/model access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4.1 now explicitly acknowledges OpenHA's existing action-space switching and distinguishes CrossHA through RL optimization of that choice. It also expands the Game-TARS description. The bibliography and dedicated related-work section remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental discussion and conclusion are substantially condensed and rewritten, and the complete case-study section moves from Section 4.5 to Appendix E. CrossAgent becomes CrossHA throughout the main prose, although the appendix and plot labels retain the old name.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from a full-width display to one column on the first page. The ablation plots are regrouped, and case-study figures move to Appendix E and are renumbered. The rollout figure uses simplified action labels and lower-resolution screenshots; table structures and plotted evidence remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity by explicitly distinguishing its contribution from OpenHA's existing switching capability and shortening repetitive experimental discussion while retaining the evidence. These gains are limited by omitted ablation-control details and inconsistent renaming. The underlying scientific results and methodological support are unchanged.
